title: Excursion operators and the spectral action, Part II: stability of the Fargues–Scholze center
summary: Plan the proof that the Fargues–Scholze spectral center acts by very stable distributions for every connected reductive group over a p-adic field. Quantitative Hecke averaging gives stability and atomic-parameter constancy; basic-inner-form detection constructs a surjection between the FS image centers and establishes compatibility with Levi restriction, stable character transfer and matching test functions. Harmonic analysis and local-shtuka trace theorems are separate imported continuations, with precise missing supplier contracts.
readme: This continuation starts with the already planned spectral-center map, semisimple parameters, normalized parabolic compatibility and coherent Hecke family. Its seven layers prove very stability by quantitative elliptic averaging and compare the FS image centers across extended pure inner forms. The reader gives exact hypotheses, all definition APIs and discriminating tests, supplier contracts G1–G3, and the stronger FS conjecture as a boundary. The full plan is research/blueprint/readmes/ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralActionPartII.md. Every layer is planned; none is claimed closed or implemented.

stages.title: Stable central distributions
stages.description: Define the stable central submodule and very stable central subalgebra; prove their action relation, the stable-character criterion for very stability and faithfulness on stable tempered virtual characters. Import stable delta_1 and harmonic-analysis separation through G1.

stages.title: Hecke operators on character spaces
stages.description: Construct Euler-class Hecke operators on finite virtual character spaces using shriek basic-stratum extensions. Prove commutation with the FS central action, stable scalar action modulo induced characters, both directed inner-form operators, their central intertwining and their e(G)e(G_b) elliptic formula. G2 supplies all finite-length and extension-convention comparisons.

stages.title: Quantitative stable averaging
stages.description: Construct the finite elliptic stable average, the dual-root sequence mu_m=4m rho_dual and normalized weight multiplicity kernels. Use the existing Weyl formula and finite Fourier basis to prove a group-uniform O(1/m) kernel error, then the discriminant-weighted compact-uniform character averaging estimate.

stages.title: Stability of the FS center
stages.description: Prove the compact stable-representative lemma and O(1/m) convergence of normalized Hecke pairings against cuspidal test functions. Deduce Hansen Theorem 1.1 by semisimple-rank induction: the FS center image lies in the very stable subalgebra for arbitrary connected reductive p-adic G.

stages.title: Atomic characters and packet parameters
stages.description: Define atomic stability by nonzero arbitrary-coefficient support minimality. Prove scalar rigidity and constancy of the FS semisimple parameter conjugacy class on atomic supports. Plan the regular supercuspidal packet corollary under Hansen’s exact tame and p-Weyl hypotheses, retaining G3 as the unresolved atomicity source input.

stages.title: Centers of extended pure inner forms
stages.description: For a basic extended pure inner form of a quasi-split G*, prove ker(Psi_G*) <= ker(Psi_G). Construct the unique surjective spectral-algebra map tau_G between the FS image centers, and prove its compatibility with normalized Levi restriction. The center maps are not asserted to identify whole stable Bernstein centers.

stages.title: Stable transfer compatibility
stages.description: Prove tau_G intertwines the FS center action with stable tempered character transfer using elliptic reverse-Hecke comparisons modulo induced characters and rank induction. Deduce that convolution preserves matching stable orbital integrals for compactly supported smooth test functions, with transfer factor e(G), including irrelevant-class vanishing.
